# PDF text rewrite captures

These CC0 synthetic input records and pinned outputs freeze a narrow text-only
observation of the migration oracle. Inputs are synthetic `PdfTextItem`
objects, not claims about strings that PDF.js itself emits. The rewrite cases
record only each output `text` value from the pinned oracle's
`normalizeItems`; they do not establish coordinate or full-field parity. The
one split/order record is separate evidence for a later pipeline integration,
not an expected result of a pure `rewrite_text` helper.

The oracle is commit `bb71f7fb0bf51dd456d27505a8c04772df182144`, package
`kordoc` 4.16.3. The source `src/pdf/text-line.ts` has SHA-256
`034b6a882eb913b723e21a1729e032bc45147e60acdf88aab655dfd415253072`.
Captures used Node v22.22.0, V8 12.4.254.21-node.33, ICU 78.2, Unicode 17.0.
The source trims first, applies per-code-point NFKC only to U+2F00–U+2FD5,
applies the permitted-character numeric rewrite with ASCII U+0020-only
deletion, then applies the rounded `fontSize >= 14` uppercase-label rewrite.
All occur before `splitEvenSpacedItem` at `text-line.ts:190–213`.

`oracle-radical-mappings.json` contains all 214 individual U+2F00–U+2FD5
results. Each mapping evaluates the source expression
`String.fromCodePoint(cp).normalize("NFKC")` directly for one scalar. In
`normalizeItems`, that exact expression is applied independently to each code
point matched by the U+2F00–U+2FD5 replacement regex; these direct captures pin
that branch without invoking later item-level stages. The 20 text rewrite
vectors above are actual `normalizeItems` captures. Every radical maps to one
output scalar of three UTF-8 bytes. A separate mixed-string capture
`Ａ⼀①⿕⿖ -> Ａ一①龠⿖` proves fullwidth Latin, circled digits, and the adjacent
out-of-range U+2FD6 are left unchanged while in-range radicals change.

The split/order evidence uses raw source sequence 1 `1 2 3` at lower y and
sequence 2 `가 나 다` at higher y. The numeric rewrite yields a single `123`;
the Hangul string passes through unchanged and the later even-spacing splitter
emits `가`, `나`, `다` at sequences 2, 2.001, and 2.002. The full function then
sorts those fragments before `123`. Later deduplication, overlap handling, and
space propagation execute in the oracle but are no-ops for these records.

The capture ran the actual `normalizeItems` source under Node's
`--experimental-strip-types`. A temporary research-only loader stubbed only
unrelated `line-detector.js` imports. Loader SHA-256:
`b43308dff5f594cab8ae385cc5efc3d390a06245270f594122eda4b44690cd54`. Temporary
capture script SHA-256: `96188c11127dae46fe2276e08246cf3f16b9967aaff8e3169272933103237cf4`.
Neither helper is checked in or required for paruster tests, packaging, or
runtime.

The workspace pins `unicode-normalization = 0.1.25` as an optional
`kordoc-pdf` dependency enabled by `pdfjs-v8` (checksum
`5fd4f6878c9cb28d874b009da9e8d183b5abc80117c40bbd187a1fde336be6e8`). Its
source reports Unicode 17.0.0. A standalone Rust probe against this crate's
`char.nfkc()` matched every one of the 214 Node outputs; both the maximum compatibility
decomposition and output were one scalar. The Node/ICU and Rust table versions
therefore align for this mapping set. The probe used rustc 1.97.0 on
`aarch64-apple-darwin`; its `main.rs` SHA-256 was
`0e31d0879d67f3d2e07ca1e2236ee6ecee9e9645c9d80d054e78ddee912765ca` and its
temporary `Cargo.toml` SHA-256 was
`653ca0d7c4a5fa2b9f1c4054fffc7dd22d66a2d9e61035617ee8c9f70d74da81`.

The stdlib-only `generate.py` recipe recreates the deterministic authored
inputs and can verify them offline:

```sh
python3 generate.py
```

Use `python3 generate.py --write` only when intentionally regenerating the
authored input records. The checked-in oracle captures are pinned data and are
not regenerated by this recipe. CC0 1.0 applies to authored inputs and
captures; oracle sources retain their own licenses.
